title: The Longest Block With Sum k

concept.title: Remember where each prefix sum appeared first
body: To get the **longest** block with sum `k` you need the **earliest** start for each end. A block ends at `j` and starts right after an earlier prefix with value `prefix[j] - k`; the earlier that prefix occurred, the longer the block. So the map stores for each prefix sum the position of its **first** occurrence only.
The map entry for the empty prefix is `0 -> -1`, so that blocks beginning at index 0 have the right length `i - (-1) = i + 1`.

statement: Given an array of `n` integers and a number `k`, find the length of the longest block of consecutive elements whose sum is exactly `k`. If there is no such block, print 0.

examples.note: The block -1 5 has sum 4 and length 2; no longer block has sum 4.

hints: Store the first position at which each prefix sum occurred.
For each end position look up `prefix - k` and measure the distance.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: The earliest occurrence of each prefix sum gives the longest block ending at the current position. Storing only first occurrences keeps the blocks as long as possible.
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

first = {0: -1}
prefix = 0
best = 0
for i in range(n):
    prefix += a[i]
    if prefix - k in first:
        best = max(best, i - first[prefix - k])
    if prefix not in first:
        first[prefix] = i
print(best)
